newsitem.title: UK: Copper slumps as metal market decline continues.
newsitem.headline: Copper slumps as metal market decline continues.

text.p: The price of copper was at its lowest for two months on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Thursday as metal market values continued to erode.
Copper dropped to $1,862 a tonne on Thursday, the lowest since July 18, after having climbed as high as $2,195 earlier this month.
Analysts said the market could now decline to test the $1,745 lows reached in late June soon after Sumitomo Corp announced heavy losses on copper trading.
"Copper has been building up to this for some time. There is very little confidence in the market, and speculators are looking to sell," a trader said.
Metal markets are suffering from a general lack of confidence, heightened by the absence of a significant pick-up in buying from end-users at the end of the summer slowdown.
Traders said losses in one metal were spilling over into other markets in the non-ferrous metals complex as well. Copper's decline was hastened by losses in aluminium on Wednesday.
Aluminium was again at two-year lows today, with business at $1,430 a tonne. A week ago this market was above $1,500, but it has been savaged by investor selling as inventories rise.
Zinc prices slipped to near the $1,000 level, while lead was in danger of falling under $800, traders said.
